title: Data that must never appear in logs, AI prompts, sample data, or source code
source: Non-Tech Change Management with AI Assistance Playbook, Sections 3 and 6
forbidden: Personal NPWP / tax ID numbers (a company NPWP or NIB is business data)
Specific personal data under UU PDP (health, biometric, genetic, criminal records, children's data, device/browsing data, and the rest of risk-criteria.json pdpRules.specific)
Customer transaction history, complaints, or feedback in identifiable form (Restricted — mask or hash)
guidance: Use fake, masked, or sample data for examples and tests; never use real production data in development. If a scan hint matches, inspect the subject and the actual value — variable names alone are not violations. An individual customer or seller name, direct email, or phone is PII even alone. A legal-entity name or generic company contact channel is business data; do not automatically exempt a named business-partner person. An internal login or access-control email alone and coordinates linked to no person do not automatically trigger this never-log list, but minimize logging; coordinates stored against an identified person are that person's personal data. Daily purchase/sales order items and values not linked to an identifiable customer are internal operational data, not sensitive financial data merely because they contain prices or are in a database; still avoid unnecessary transaction detail in logs. 'npwp' matches need a subject check: a company NPWP is business data. 'address' means a home or postal address, not email_address, ip_address, mac_address, wallet/contract address, or a memory address. 'phone' means a real subscriber number, not a UI label or country-code lookup. See risk-criteria.json for the full classification rule.
